items.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021
items.q: Interviewer mentions Louis Armstrong in a quote from Harry 'Sweets' Edison; Interviewee responds 'Yeah. I can resonate with that.'

ctx.x: amazing stuff you’ve ever heard, and the most creative stuff, and just being like I want to be able to do that but on the saxophone. And so then slowly over the years progressing and adding — oh wonder if I could get — I had this pop sound, I wonder if I could kind of get a hi-hat sound, and then thinking, also thinking of other instruments I’ve explored. I’ve played drumset a little bit and thinking okay so where’s my bass drum sound? Where’s my snare? Okay could I do like a roll sound? And then okay I have a…

All right. Well speaking of sweet spot, your description of developing your thing reminded me of a quote. I was able to interview Harry “Sweets” Edison, the trumpet player from the Basie era. And he was talking about when he was a young man, this would have been the late 1930s, he said this about the already-established musicians like Louis Armstrong and Coleman Hawkins. And what he said was, “Everybody had a sound of their own, a sound that could be recognized. That was our ambition in my day, to not © Fillius…
be an imitator, but an originator. We would rather be the world’s worst originator than the world’s greatest imitator.
